records.prompt: give me a 3-day beginner workout plan, keep it short (Day 1, Day 2, Day 3)
records.answer:
**3-Day Full-Body Beginner Plan** — one rest day between sessions (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri). Full body each day is the right split at 3 days/week: you hit each muscle 3×/week, which is the fastest way to learn the lifts and grow as a beginner.

**Warm-up (every day):** 5 min easy bike/row + 2–3 ramp-up sets on the first lift (empty bar → ~50% → ~75% of your working weight).

**Day 1**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RPE | Rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goblet or back squat | 3 × 8–12 | 7 | 2 min |
| Push-up (knees or incline ok) | 3 × 8–12 | 7–8 | 90 s |
| One-arm dumbbell row | 3 × 8–12 /side | 7 | 90 s |
| Plank | 3 × 20–40 s | 7 | 60 s |

**Day 2**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RPE | Rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| Romanian deadlift (DB or bar) | 3 × 8–12 | 7 | 2 min |
| Dumbbell bench press | 3 × 8–12 | 7 | 90 s |
| Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up | 3 × 8–12 | 7 | 90 s |
| Standing DB shoulder press | 2 × 10–12 | 7–8 | 90 s |

**Day 3**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | RPE | Rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| Leg press or split squat | 3 × 8–12 | 7 | 2 min |
| Seated cable row | 3 × 8–12 | 7 | 90 s |
| DB incline press | 3 × 8–12 | 7 | 90 s |
| Face pull | 2 × 12–15 | 7 | 60 s |
| Dead bug | 2 × 8–10 /side | 7 | 60 s |

**Progression (double progression):** stay in the rep range. When you hit the top of the range on all sets at your target RPE, add the smallest increment — 2.5 kg upper body, 5 kg lower body — and drop back to the bottom of the range.

records.answer:
**3-Day Beginner Full Body** (train Mon/Wed/Fri or any 3 non-consecutive days — a day of rest between sessions lets you recover, which is where the growth actually happens.)

Warm-up every session: 5 min easy cardio + 2–3 ramp-up sets on the first lift (empty bar → build to your working weight). Rest 90–120 s on compounds, 60–90 s on singles. All sets @ RPE 7–8 (1–3 reps left in the tank).

**Day 1**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Goblet squat or leg press | 3 × 8–12 |
| Push-up (knees or incline if needed) | 3 × 8–12 |
| One-arm dumbbell row | 3 × 10–12 |
| Plank | 3 × 20–40 s |

**Day 2**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Romanian deadlift (dumbbells or barbell) | 3 × 8–10 |
| Dumbbell bench press | 3 × 8–12 |
| Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up | 3 × 10–12 |
| Dumbbell shoulder press | 2 × 10–12 |

**Day 3**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Hip bridge / glute bridge | 3 × 10–15 |
| Split squat (rear foot elevated when ready) | 2 × 8–10/leg |
| Seated cable row | 3 × 10–12 |
| Face pull | 2 × 12–15 |
| Dead bug | 3 × 8/side |

**Progression (double progression):** stay in the rep range; when *all* sets hit the top of the range at RPE 8, add 2.5 kg upper / 5 kg lower and drop back to the bottom of the range. Deload every 6–8 weeks: same weights, cut total sets ~40%.

**Track per set:** date, exercise, weight, reps, RPE. That's enough to see weekly volume and est. 1RM (weight × (1 + reps/30)) climb over time.

~10 hard sets per muscle per week sits right at the beginner sweet spot — enough stimulus, recoverable. If something hurts sharply (not just muscle burn), stop that lift and get it checked by a physio rather than pushing through.
